arxiv-2012-14711.title: A low-mass binary neutron star: long-term ejecta evolution and kilonovae with weak blue emission
arxiv-2012-14711.creator: Kyohei Kawaguchi, Sho Fujibayashi, Masaru Shibata, Masaomi Tanaka, Shinya Wanajo
arxiv-2012-14711.description: Abstract We study the long-term evolution of ejecta formed in a binary neutron star (BNS) merger that results in a long-lived remnant NS by performing a hydrodynamics simulation with the outflow data of a numerical relativity simulation as the initial condition. At the homologously expanding phase, the total ejecta mass reaches ≈ 0.1 ​ M ⊙ \approx 0.

arxiv-2101-02447.title: Practical Evaluation of Out-of-Distribution Detection Methods for Image Classification
arxiv-2101-02447.creator: Engkarat Techapanurak, Takayuki Okatani
arxiv-2101-02447.description: Abstract We reconsider the evaluation of OOD detection methods for image recognition. Although many studies have been conducted so far to build better OOD detection methods, most of them follow Hendrycks and Gimpel’s work for the method of experimental evaluation.

arxiv-2112-05688.title: Mapping the metal-insulator phase diagram by algebraically fast-forwarding dynamics on a cloud quantum computer
arxiv-2112-05688.creator: Thomas Steckmann, Trevor Keen, Efekan Kökcü, Alexander F. Kemper, Eugene F. Dumitrescu, Yan Wang
arxiv-2112-05688.description: Abstract Dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) maps the local Green’s function of the Hubbard model to that of the Anderson impurity model and thus gives an approximate solution of the Hubbard model from the solution of simpler quantum impurity model. Accurate solutions to the Anderson impurity model nonetheless become intractable for large systems.

arxiv-2201-02839.title: Ill-posedness for the Camassa-Holm equation in B p , 1 1 ∩ C 0 , 1 B_{p,1}^{1}\cap C^{0,1}
arxiv-2201-02839.creator: Jinlu Li, Yanghai Yu, Yingying Guo, Weipeng Zhu
arxiv-2201-02839.description: Abstract Abstract: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem for the Camassa-Holm equation on the real line. By presenting a new construction of initial data, we show that the solution map in the smaller space B_{p,1}^{1}\cap C^{0,1} with p\in(2,\infty] is discontinuous at origin.

arxiv-2201-12513.title: The Geography of Facebook Groups in the United States To be presented at ICWSM 2023.
arxiv-2201-12513.creator: Amaç Herdağdelen, Lada Adamic, Bogdan State
arxiv-2201-12513.description: Abstract We present a de-identified and aggregated dataset based on geographical patterns of Facebook Groups usage and demonstrate its association with measures of social capital. The dataset is aggregated at United States county level. Established spatial measures of social capital are known to vary across US counties. Their availability and recency depends on running costly surveys.

arxiv-2202-00795.title: Disaster Tweets Classification using BERT-Based Language Model
arxiv-2202-00795.creator: Anh Duc Le
arxiv-2202-00795.description: Abstract Social networking services have became an important communication channel in time of emergency. The aim of this study is to create a machine learning language model that is able to investigate if a person or area was in danger or not. The ubiquitousness of smartphones enables people to announce an emergency they’re observing in real-time.

arxiv-2305-18864.title: Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics Based on Quantization with Increasing Resolution
arxiv-2305-18864.creator: Jinwuk Seok, Changsik Cho
arxiv-2305-18864.description: Abstract Stochastic learning dynamics based on Langevin or Levy stochastic differential equations (SDEs) in deep neural networks control the variance of noise by varying the size of the mini-batch or directly those of injecting noise. Since the noise variance affects the approximation performance, the design of the additive noise is significant in SDE-based learning and practical implementation.

arxiv-2307-03062.title: Quantum criticality on a compressible lattice
arxiv-2307-03062.creator: Saheli Sarkar ∗, Lars Franke ∗, Nikolas Grivas, Markus Garst
arxiv-2307-03062.description: Abstract The stability of a quantum critical point in the O ⁡ ( N ) O(N) universality class with respect to an elastic coupling, that preserves O ⁡ ( N ) O(N) symmetry, is investigated for isotropic elasticity in the framework of the renormalization group (RG) close to the upper critical dimension d = 3 − ϵ d=3-\epsilon .

arxiv-2309-02162.title: Advancing Text-to-GLOSS Neural Translation Using a Novel Hyper-parameter Optimization Technique
arxiv-2309-02162.creator: Ouargani Younes El Khattabi Noussaima
arxiv-2309-02162.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the use of transformers for Neural Machine Translation of text-to-GLOSS for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing communication. Due to the scarcity of available data and limited resources for text-to-GLOSS translation, we treat the problem as a low-resource language task.

arxiv-2401-05854.title: Impact of molecular properties on diffraction at nanomasks with low charge density
arxiv-2401-05854.creator: Ksenija Simonović, Richard Ferstl, Anders Barlow, Armin Shayeghi, Christian Brand, Markus Arndt
arxiv-2401-05854.description: Abstract The quantum wave nature of matter is a cornerstone of modern physics, which has been demonstrated for a wide range of fundamental and composite particles. While diffraction at nanomechanical masks is usually regarded to be independent of atomic or molecular internal states, the particles’ polarisabilities and dipole moments lead to dispersive interactions with the grating surface.

arxiv-2407-09975.title: The GPT Surprise: Offering Large Language Model Chat in a Massive Coding Class Reduced Engagement but Increased Adopters’ Exam Performances
arxiv-2407-09975.creator: Allen Nie, Yash Chandak, Miroslav Suzara, Ali Malik, Juliette Woodrow, Matt Peng, Mehran Sahami, Emma Brunskill, Chris Piech
arxiv-2407-09975.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are quickly being adopted in a wide range of learning experiences, especially via ubiquitous and broadly accessible chat interfaces like ChatGPT and Copilot. This type of interface is readily available to students and teachers around the world, yet relatively little research has been done to assess the impact of such generic tools on student learning.

arxiv-2412-19987.title: DELAYED RANDOM PARTIAL GRADIENT AVERAGING FOR FEDERATED LEARNING
arxiv-2412-19987.creator: Xinyi Hu
arxiv-2412-19987.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xinyi Hu. Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that enables multiple clients to train a shared model collaboratively while preserving privacy. However, the scaling of real-world FL systems is often limited by two communication bottlenecks: (a) while the increasing computing power of edge devices enables the deployment of large-scale Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), the limited bandwidth constraints frequent transmissions over large DNNs; and (b) high latency cost greatly degrades the performance of FL.

arxiv-2502-18469.title: Using LLM-Based Approaches to Enhance and Automate Topic Labeling
arxiv-2502-18469.creator: Trishia Khandelwal
arxiv-2502-18469.description: Abstract Topic modeling has become a crucial method for analyzing text data, particularly for extracting meaningful insights from large collections of documents. However, the output of these models typically consists of lists of keywords that require manual interpretation for precise labeling.

arxiv-2503-14785.title: SEEK: Self-adaptive Explainable Kernel For Nonstationary Gaussian Processes
arxiv-2503-14785.creator: Nima Negarandeh †, Carlos Mora, Ramin Bostanabad
arxiv-2503-14785.description: Abstract Abstract Gaussian processes (GPs) are powerful probabilistic models that define flexible priors over functions, offering strong interpretability and uncertainty quantification. However, GP models often rely on simple, stationary kernels which can lead to suboptimal predictions and miscalibrated uncertainty estimates, especially in nonstationary real-world applications.

arxiv-2508-14247.title: Time-optimal Asynchronous Minimal Vertex Covering by Myopic Robots on Graph
arxiv-2508-14247.creator: Saswata Jana, Subhajit Pramanick, Adri Bhattacharya, Partha Sarathi Mandal
arxiv-2508-14247.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Saswata Jana, Subhajit Pramanick, Adri Bhattacharya, Partha Sarathi Mandal. In a connected graph with an autonomous robot swarm with limited visibility, it is natural to ask whether the robots can be deployed to certain vertices satisfying a given property using only local knowledge. This paper affirmatively answers the question with a set of myopic (finite visibility range) luminous robots with the aim of filling a minimal vertex cover (MVC) of a given graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) .

arxiv-2509-18189.title: Qianfan-VL: Domain-Enhanced Universal Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2509-18189.creator: Qianfan Team, Baidu AI Cloud
arxiv-2509-18189.description: Abstract We present Qianfan-VL, a series of multimodal large language models ranging from 3B to 70B parameters, achieving state-of-the-art performance through innovative domain enhancement techniques. Our approach employs multi-stage progressive training and high-precision data synthesis pipelines, which prove to be critical technologies for enhancing domain-specific capabilities while maintaining strong general performance.

arxiv-2509-22113.title: Countering adversarial evasion in regression analysis
arxiv-2509-22113.creator: [1ex] David Benfield, Phan Tu Vuong, Alain Zemkoho, [1.5ex] School of Mathematical SciencesUniversity of SouthamptonSO17 1BJ Southampton, United Kingdom db3g17@soton.ac.uk , t.v.phan@soton.ac.uk , a.b.zemkoho@soton.ac.uk [1.5ex]
arxiv-2509-22113.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by [1ex] David Benfield, Phan Tu Vuong, Alain Zemkoho, [1.5ex] School of Mathematical SciencesUniversity of SouthamptonSO17 1BJ Southampton, United Kingdom db3g17@soton.ac.uk , t.v.phan@soton.ac.uk , a.b.zemkoho@soton.ac.uk [1.5ex]. Adversarial machine learning challenges the assumption that the underlying distribution remains consistent throughout the training and implementation of a prediction model.

arxiv-2512-18471.title: The Geometry of Abstraction: Continual Learning via Recursive Quotienting
arxiv-2512-18471.creator: Xin Li, Department of Computer ScienceUniversity at Albany xli48@albany.edu
arxiv-2512-18471.description: Abstract Continual learning systems operating in fixed-dimensional spaces face a fundamental geometric barrier: the flat manifold problem. When experience is represented as a linear trajectory in Euclidean space, the geodesic distance between temporal events grows linearly with time, forcing the required covering number (capacity) to diverge. In fixed-dimensional hardware, the volume expansion inevitably forces trajectory overlap, manifesting as catastrophic interference.

arxiv-2602-15906.title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Networks for Approximating PDE Flow Maps
arxiv-2602-15906.creator: Nahid Binandeh Dehaghani, Ban Q. Tran, Rafal Wisniewski, Susan Mengel, A. Pedro Aguiar
arxiv-2602-15906.description: Abstract We investigate quantum-inspired tensor networks (QTNs) for approximating flow maps of hydrodynamic partial differential equations (PDEs). Motivated by the effective low-rank structure that emerges after tensorization of discretized transport and diffusion dynamics, we encode PDE states as matrix product states (MPS) and represent the evolution operator as a structured low-rank matrix product operator (MPO) in tensor-train form (e.g.

arxiv-2605-22275.title: Adaptive Measurement Allocation for Learning Kernelized SVMs Under Noisy Observations
arxiv-2605-22275.creator: Artur Miroszewski

pmc-10725610.title: Advancing psychiatry trainee wellbeing and safety: Building on RANZCP Position Statement 48
pmc-10725610.creator: Michael James Weightman, Andrew Amos, Edward Miller
pmc-10725610.description: ObjectiveThe RANZCP recently released Position Statement 48 on the ‘safety and wellbeing of psychiatrists and those in psychiatry training’. This article will examine the five key domains highlighted by this statement and provide suggestions on how this guidance might relate to trainees.

pmc-10958995.title: Predicting Waist Circumference From a Single Computed Tomography Image Using a Mobile App (Measure It): Development and Evaluation Study
pmc-10958995.creator: Abderrahmen Masmoudi, Amine Zouari, Ahmed Bouzid, Kais Fourati, Soulaimen Baklouti, Mohamed Ben Amar, Salah Boujelben
pmc-10958995.description: BackgroundDespite the existing evidence that waist circumference (WC) provides independent and additive information to BMI when predicting morbidity and mortality, this measurement is not routinely obtained in clinical practice. Using computed tomography (CT) scan images, mobile health (mHealth) has the potential to make this abdominal obesity parameter easily available even in retrospective studies.

pmc-12534946.title: A nomogram for predicting ICU mortality of sepsis associated encephalopathy: a retrospective cohort study based on MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD
pmc-12534946.creator: Xuemei Hu, Jianbao Wang, Shaowei Wang, Tianfeng Hua, Min Yang
pmc-12534946.description: BackgroundSepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a fatal complication of sepsis, with a high mortality rate worldwide. This study aimed to reduce mortality and improve the quality of life of patients with SAEs by developing a practical nomogram to predict the risk factors associated with ICU mortality.

pmc-12552201.title: Effects of pearl millet diet on serum micronutrient status, mental health and meta-cognitive skills in athletes: a randomised controlled trial
pmc-12552201.creator: Kommi Kalpana, Alisha Saifi, Gulshan Lal Khanna, Dayakar Benhur Rao, Gurseen Rakhra, Ekta Tanwar
pmc-12552201.description: BackgroundMental health challenges, including anxiety, stress, depression, sleep disturbance and cognitive deficits, are prevalent among athletes due to continuous overtraining or field stress. Pearl millet is a nutrient-dense grain rich in lipids, iron, dietary fibre, and B vitamins and has potential benefits for mental well-being and improved cognitive function.

pmc-12663042.title: Unsupervised Random Forest Identifies Important Genetic Prognostic Factors for Breast Cancer Survival Time
pmc-12663042.creator: Benjamin Goldberg, Eric Nels Pederson, Zhengqing Ouyang
pmc-12663042.description: Objective:Breast cancer is one of the most prominent and deadly diseases in the world, and its prognosis varies widely based on the expression of certain genes. Identification of these genes is important for developing and interpreting clinical prognostic tests as well as furthering our understanding of breast cancer biology.

pmc-12664164.title: Exercise as a modulator of systemic inflammation and oxidative stress biomarkers across clinical and healthy populations: an umbrella meta-analysis
pmc-12664164.creator: Wei Feng, Yanzhong Wang, Xin Gu, Duonan Yu, Zhiwei Liu
pmc-12664164.description: ObjectiveInflammation is a condition that trigger an immune response and oxidative stress refers to an imbalance between production and elimination of reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, several non-pharmacological approaches have been proposed to improve health outcomes, among which exercise programs have shown promising effects on inflammatory and oxidative biomarkers across various health conditions.

pmc-13072465.title: Impact of combined unilateral mastectomy and ovariohysterectomy on acute phase response and wound healing in dogs with mammary gland tumors
pmc-13072465.creator: Grisnarong Wongbandue, Phirom Prompiram, Panyakamol Chandrasakha, Nawarus Prapaiwan
pmc-13072465.description: BackgroundCanine mammary gland tumors (CMTs) are among the most common neoplasms in female dogs, and surgical excision is the standard modality for treatment of CMTs. Unilateral mastectomy (UM) is frequently combined with ovariohysterectomy (OVH), which may lead to different levels of systemic inflammation and wound-healing.

pmc-13122892.title: Novel LUC7L::NUTM1 fusion in PDGFRA-rearranged myeloproliferative neoplasm with eosinophilia: a case report
pmc-13122892.creator: Jing Zhou, Hanbing Yao, Jiarong Ren, Ke Sun, Dongxue Chen, Rui Zhang, Gangfeng Wang
pmc-13122892.description: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with PDGFRA rearrangement are a group of haematologic tumors, in which the clonal proliferation of precursor eosinophils leads to persistent eosinophilic hyperplasia, and varying degrees of involvement of the liver, spleen and lymph nodes. While PDGFRA rearrangements are frequently observed in mpn-eo, the co-occurrence of t(15;16)(q14;p13) translocations leading to LUC7L::NUTM1 fusion genes has not been previously documented.

pmc-13330163.title: Effectiveness of an educational intervention in enhancing parents’ knowledge, perception, and acceptability of human papillomavirus vaccine
pmc-13330163.creator: Nawal Abdulghani, Safah Faqih, Asayil Alqurashi, Kamilya Baljon
pmc-13330163.description: BackgroundCervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, largely caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV). The HPV vaccine has been proven to effectively reduce HPV infection rates and cervical cancer risk, making vaccination a crucial preventive measure.

pmc-13333496.title: Effects of enteral immunonutrition on postoperative complications of colorectal cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13333496.creator: Yuhang Wu, Qingyu Du, Chenglin Zhao, Guo Zu

pmc-13413183.title: Effectiveness of Manual Lymphatic Drainage After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review
pmc-13413183.creator: Papi Davide, Carulli Christian, Lorenzoni Niccolo’, Montigiani Giulia
pmc-13413183.description: Background/Objectives: Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA) is the gold-standard treatment for end-stage knee osteoarthritis. After surgery, the natural onset of edema and pain usually influences the early functional recovery. Manual Lymphatic Drainage (MLD) has been proposed as a possible adjunct rehabilitation strategy in the immediate management of the operated joint.

pmc-13621319.title: Sulfur signaling: from molecules to physiological responses
pmc-13621319.creator: Stanislav Kopriva, Hideki Takahashi, Markus Wirtz
pmc-13621319.description: ty, pathogen attack, and oxidative stress. Unlike other mineral nutrients, sulfur is incorporated into a uniquely diverse set of bioactive molecules whose functions extend far beyond features attributed to the primary metabolites. This biochemical versatility makes sulfur not only indispensable for growth but also a key component of the adaptive capacity of plants in the face of dynamic environmental challenges.
